heading: Extend until last occurrence
body:
Can't close a segment mid-character. If you see 'a' at index 0 and 'a' appears again at index 5, the segment **must** extend to at least index 5.

**Strategy:** Precompute last index of every char, then scan left-to-right tracking the farthest "must-reach" point.

heading: When i == end, cut
body:
Track `end = max(end, last[c])` as you scan. When your current index **equals** `end`, you've satisfied all constraints — no character in this segment appears later.

That's your cut point. Record segment length, then start fresh.

label: Crux · Python

q: Why do we precompute the last occurrence of each character instead of searching for it during the main scan?
options: To avoid O(n²) time complexity from repeatedly scanning forward
To use more memory and make the code more complex
To ensure segments are sorted in ascending order
explain: Precomputing avoids repeatedly searching forward for each character's last occurrence, which would degrade to O(n²).
